current.text: Portland brought back Damian Lillard, added Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday, and gets a full season of Scoot Henderson. The team also has a new, first-time head coach.

Experts agree his usage and assists will drop with Lillard, Morant, Holiday and Henderson handling the ball. He is no longer the main point forward and becomes the third distributor in the starting group.
Projections put his usage at about 24 to 26 percent and his scoring at around 20 points per game. His assists should fall below 7 per game.
He is a projected starter at forward. Portland is short on forwards, and the rotation is thin after the eighth man.
His minutes and role are seen as safe even with the drop in usage.
Sharpe being out should help Avdija, but a full repeat of last season is not expected.

The newest call projects him around 46th. The right spot is round three, more likely round four, and never round two. Mock drafts agree: round 4 or picks 44 to 49 are fair, and pick 34 to 36 is too early. ESPN's rank of 60 is too low.
In an auction mock draft, an expert who is lower on him than others bought him for 23 USD and did not see it as an overpay.
He shot under 32 percent from three last season and got worse late in the season, partly because of a back injury.
Lower usage might bring his three-point shooting back up.
Portland plays 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, a weak total, with three back-to-backs in those weeks. The team has 15 back-to-backs this season and a five-game week starting February 8.

durable.text: His fantasy profile is assists plus above-average rebounds for a forward. Free throws are not his selling point.
At his best he is a relentless downhill driver and passer.
His value depends on high usage. His percentages are iffy, and his line needed a huge on-ball role.
Turnovers are his clear weak category, far worse than the league pool and his position.
He had a back injury last season, and he played poorly after it.

note: Experts agree he loses usage and assists to Lillard, Morant, Holiday and Henderson. The newest call puts him around 46th, a round three to four player, which fits a price near our league's 17 USD from last season and the Yahoo average cost of 17. A mock auction paid 23 USD, and Yahoo's 24 USD value is the ceiling. With about 3.3 turnovers per game he fits punt TO builds best, and he still gives frontcourt assists and rebounds. Early in the season, check his assist and usage numbers next to Lillard and Morant, whether his three-point shooting recovers, and how long Sharpe is out. Portland's weak 10-game playoff schedule is a reason to sell him before the 2027-03-04 deadline if his value holds.
